title: The first Americans and the colonies
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 4). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
facts: American Indians, also called Native Americans, lived in America for thousands of years before the Europeans arrived.
In 1492, Christopher Columbus, an explorer from Italy, sailed from Spain and reached the Americas. After that, many more Europeans came.
There are many American Indian tribes, like the Cherokee, Navajo, Sioux, Apache and Hopi.
Many tribes still live in the United States today.

newWords.meaning: a group of people who share a history and a way of life
land set aside for American Indian tribes

story.say: American Indians, also called Native Americans, lived in America for thousands of years.

help.simpler: The first people in America were American Indians.
help.example: Both names are right: American Indians or Native Americans.
help.why: The test asks who lived in America before the Europeans arrived.

story.say: They lived here long before the Europeans arrived.

help.simpler: American Indians were here first. Europeans came much later.
help.example: Europeans are people from countries like Spain, Britain and France.
help.why: “American Indians” or “Native Americans” is the answer on the test.

check.prompt: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?

story.say: In 1492, Christopher Columbus, an explorer from Italy, sailed from Spain and reached the Americas.

help.simpler: Columbus was a European explorer. He reached the Americas in 1492.
help.example: He was born in Italy, but the king and queen of Spain paid for his trip.
help.why: It helps you remember that Europeans came after American Indians.

story.say: After that, many more Europeans came.

help.simpler: Columbus came first. Then many other Europeans followed.
help.example: People came from Spain, Britain, France and other countries.
help.why: This is how the time of the colonies began.

check.statement: Christopher Columbus was an American Indian.

story.say: There are many American Indian tribes, like the Cherokee, Navajo, Sioux, Apache and Hopi.

help.simpler: A tribe is a group of American Indian people with a shared history.
help.example: The Navajo and the Hopi are two tribes in the Southwest.
help.why: The test asks you to name one American Indian tribe.

story.say: Many tribes still live in the United States today.

help.simpler: American Indian tribes are part of the country today, too.
help.example: Some tribes live on reservations: land that belongs to the tribe.
help.why: Any one tribe on the official list is a right answer.

check.prompt: Name one American Indian tribe in the United States.

listen.explanationKey: The colonists came to America for many reasons. Name one.
facts: A colony is a place ruled by a country far away. The American colonies were groups of towns, farms and cities along the Atlantic coast, ruled by Britain.
People came from Europe to live in the American colonies.
They came for many reasons: freedom, religious freedom, economic opportunity, or to escape persecution.
There were 13 colonies. They became the 13 original states, like Virginia, New York, Massachusetts, Pennsylvania and Georgia.

newWords.meaning: a person who lives in a colony
a chance to do something good
cruel treatment, often for your religion or ideas

story.say: A colony is a place ruled by a country far away.

help.simpler: A colony belongs to another country across the sea.
help.example: The American colonies were ruled from Britain, far across the ocean.
help.why: Knowing this word helps with many history questions.

story.say: The American colonies were towns, farms and cities along the Atlantic coast, ruled by Britain.

help.simpler: The colonies were on the east side of America, by the ocean.
help.example: Boston and Philadelphia were cities in the colonies.
help.why: Later, these colonies became the United States.

check.statement: The American colonies were ruled by Britain.

story.say: People came from Europe to live in the colonies. They came for many reasons.

help.simpler: Colonists were people from Europe who lived in the colonies.
help.example: Families crossed the ocean by ship to start a new life.
help.why: The test asks you to name one reason the colonists came.

story.say: Some came for freedom, or for religious freedom.

help.simpler: Some people wanted to pray in their own way, without fear.
help.example: Religious freedom means you can follow any religion, or none.
help.why: “Freedom” and “religious freedom” are both answers on the test.

story.say: Some came for economic opportunity, or to escape persecution.

help.simpler: Some wanted better work. Some wanted to get away from unfair treatment.
help.example: Economic opportunity: a chance to own land, work and earn money.
help.why: “Economic opportunity” and “escape persecution” are answers too.

check.prompt: Tap the reason that means a chance to work and earn money.

story.say: There were 13 colonies. They became the 13 original states.

help.simpler: The 13 colonies became the first 13 states.
help.example: Today there are 50 states. The first 13 were the colonies.
help.why: The test asks you to name five of the 13 original states.

story.say: Virginia, New York, Massachusetts, Pennsylvania and Georgia were five of them.

help.simpler: These five are easy to remember. They were all colonies.
help.example: Georgia was in the south. Massachusetts was in the north.
help.why: You can name these five on the test.

check.prompt: Which one was one of the 13 original states?

readIt.sentence: Why do people want to come to America?

writeIt.sentence: People come to the United States to be free.
